name: Diagnostic_INT-PRT_2
generalfeedback:
For this question we will use integration by parts. Remembering that the formula is: \[\int u\,\frac{dv}{dt}\,dt = uv - \int v\,\frac{du}{dt}\,dt.\] Now we want to find \(\int {{CT:2}}\,d{{CT:3}}\). So, we let \[ u = {{CT:3}}^2\quad\Rightarrow\quad \frac{du}{d{{CT:3}}} = 2{{CT:3}},\] and \[ \frac{dv}{dt} = {{CT:4}}\quad\Rightarrow\quad v = {{CT:5}}.\] We can now substitute these into the formula to find that: \[ \int {{CT:2}}\,d{{CT:3}} = {{CT:6}} - \int {{CT:7}}\,d{{CT:3}}. \] We now have to perform an integration by parts again on what we have found.

This time:

\[ u = 2{{CT:3}}\quad\Rightarrow\quad \frac{du}{d{{CT:3}}}=2,\] and \[\frac{dv}{dt} = {{CT:5}}\quad\Rightarrow\quad v={{CT:8}}. \] So we get: \[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \int {{CT:2}}\,d{{CT:3}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:6}} - \int {{CT:7}}\,d{{CT:3}}, \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:6}} - \left({{CT:9}} - 2\int {{CT:8}}\,d{{CT:3}}\right). \end{array}\] Which means: \[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \int {{CT:2}}\,d{{CT:3}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:6}} - \left({{CT:9}} - ({{CT:10}})\right),\\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:11}} + constant . \end{array}\]
